topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes and introducing the framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms and oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt signaling pathways that allow cancer cells to sustain proliferation independently of external growth cues.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic disruptions halt terminal differentiation in both hematopoietic malignancies and solid intestinal carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis, cellular senescence, and replicative limits
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how cancer cells overcome cell death and proliferative limits by disrupting apoptotic machinery, reactivating telomerase, and disabling p53-mediated stress responses.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the metabolic adaptations of cancer cells, including the Warburg effect and Krebs cycle enzyme mutations that generate oncometabolites and drive tumor progression.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the requirement of vascular supply for tumor growth, the timing of the angiogenic switch, and the balance of pro- and anti-angiogenic signals.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the multistep invasion-metastasis cascade, clinical monitoring of circulating tumor cells, the seed and soil hypothesis, and the genomic drivers of metastatic colonization.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks on cancer hallmark complexity and housekeeping information for the practicals.
